extracted.intended_audience: general readers, potential authors, librarians, and mathematicians interested in the journal
extracted.subtask_description: Describes The Mathematical Intelligencer's editorial aims, scope, content types, publication details, and notable editorial practices — useful for potential contributors, readers, and librarians assessing fit. Summarizes the journal's history, reception, and recurring features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims at a conversational and scholarly tone, rather than the technical and specialist tone more common among academic journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly contrasts the Intelligencer's conversational/scholarly voice with more technical specialist journals. Related notes: volumes are released quarterly and a subset of articles is open access; some articles have been cross-published in Scientific American. Editors have described the purpose as 'to inform, to entertain, and to provoke.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed contribution types
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes a variety of contributions: articles of a strictly mathematical nature, shorter 'notes,' poetry, short fiction, interviews, and regular columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article names specific regular columns (history 'Years Ago', humor 'Mathematically Bent', 'Mathematical Gems and Curiosities', 'Mathematical Communities', 'The Mathematical Tourist', 'Stamp Corner') and notes long-time contributors and column editors. This indicates openness to nontraditional mathematical formats (poetry, fiction, columns) as well as expository pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial willingness to engage controversial topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost from the beginning, the journal's editors have shown a 'willingness to deal with controversial topics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives examples where editors published or excerpted provocative material (e.g., Morris Kline excerpt, Steven Krantz book review on fractals, debates around the variability hypothesis) and notes that editors saw controversies as making interesting reading. For prospective authors, this signals the journal may accept provocative/expository commentary and debate pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: emphasis on front-line/expository content rather than original technical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Has been described as a journal that publishes articles about front-line research rather than research per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reception commentary suggests the Intelligencer favors exposition, historical pieces, and broadly accessible discussions of current mathematical themes rather than specialist, technical research papers. This is a criterion for fit: submissions should be accessible and of general interest to mathematically inclined readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication particulars (publisher, frequency, identifiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published by Springer Science+Business Media; volumes released quarterly; some articles open access. ISSN numbers provided (print and web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical notes: started informally in 1971, volumes resumed with volume 0 in 1977 and volume 1 in 1978; editorial succession and current co-editors-in-chief are listed. These details are relevant for citation, submission timing, and archival/library considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book review coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The book review section covers books, both non-fiction and fiction, of interest to the mathematically inclined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under editor John McCleary the book review section covers both non-fiction and fiction. This signals that reviews need not be strictly technical and can cover broadly mathematical or mathematically themed literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular columns and recurring features
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains a set of regular columns and recurring features on topics like history of mathematics, humor, mathematical curiosities, mathematical communities, travel ('The Mathematical Tourist'), and mathematics on stamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named column editors and long-time contributors are listed (e.g., Robin Wilson for 'Stamp Corner', Colin Adams for 'Mathematically Bent'). For prospective contributors, these recurring formats indicate established venues within the journal for shorter or themed pieces and potential editorial contacts.
